Intellectual disability and fifth-digit bone/nail hypoplasia define CSS; visual impairment occurs in 30–79%. Cardiac abnormalities (30–79%) omitted at cap.
Overgrowth of the mandibular condyle affects the temporomandibular joint; secondary malocclusion does not establish direct dental damage.
Usually bacterial infection of the endometrium; reproductive anatomy has no organ axis, but infection supplies the mechanism axis.
Immune-mediated axial and peripheral arthritis beginning in childhood; uveitis is not established above the 30% threshold for this subtype.
The defining syndrome combines intellectual disability/seizures, corneal keratoconus, and sinoatrial conduction block.
Progressive cerebellar and pyramidal dysfunction; abnormal saccades and torticollis are neurologic manifestations, not separate eye or muscle damage.
Developmental delay, seizures and brain dysmyelination define the disorder; strabismus is described as common and impairs ocular alignment.
Chronic actinomycotic infection of the lacrimal canaliculi, supported by the lacrimal and eye-infection parents.
Deficient hypothalamic or pituitary stimulation causes adrenal cortisol deficiency; central hormonal origin does not itself establish neurologic damage.
Localized chronic inflammatory dermatosis characterized by immune-mediated cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis.
Immune lymphoproliferation/cytopenias; renal failure 1/3, nephropathy 1/1; hepatomegaly 2/2 with transaminitis 1/1. Arthritis 1/3 omitted at cap; small samples.
Origin is mediastinal adipose tissue, outside the specified axes; no lung, pleural, cardiac, subcutaneous or locomotor tissue origin is established.
Granulomatous lesions directly affect genital/anoperineal skin with ulcers and lymphoedema; intestinal disease and a specific immune mechanism are not established.
Renal tubular failure to excrete free water defines the disorder and causes hypotonic hyponatremia; seizures need not indicate lasting neurologic damage.
Necrosis directly destroys pituitary endocrine tissue; ischemic origin alone does not establish a separate vascular disorder.
Calcifying thrombotic vasculopathy primarily affects cardiac and pulmonary viscera, causing fibrosis and necrosis; underlying renal disease is separate.
Lysosomal metabolic disease with progressive neurologic dysfunction; skeletal disease is common, with kyphoscoliosis/platyspondyly in 1/1 and pes cavus in 1/3.
Primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy comprises periostosis/arthropathy with clubbing and variable pachydermia; common cardiac involvement is not established.
Nontraumatic atlantoaxial rotatory subluxation; preceding infection or surgery is a trigger, not an additional organ manifestation.
Sulfur amino-acid metabolic disorder defined by progressive encephalopathy, seizures and lens dislocation; ectopia lentis occurs in 80–99%.
Chronic immune-mediated airway disease; absence of type-2 inflammation does not remove asthma's immune mechanism.
Autoinflammatory periodic fever; sensorineural hearing impairment reported in 2/3. Urticaria and arthralgia are episodic; splenomegaly alone shows no dysfunction.
Serine biosynthesis deficiency is a neurometabolic disorder; severe skin and skeletal anomalies of Neu-Laxova syndrome do not apply across the umbrella.
Progressive Friedreich neurologic degeneration with retained reflexes; cardiac and skeletal involvement is reduced in this variant and not established here at ≥30%.
